title: Workers: Unclear how to set fetch client for classic/module worker scripts
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

In [`run a worker`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#run-a-worker), step 6 has us create a new `agent` for the worker:

> 6.  Let agent be the result of [obtaining a dedicated/shared worker agent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#obtain-a-dedicated/shared-worker-agent) given outside settings and is shared. Run the rest of these steps in that agent.

It's my understanding (which could be way off) that this new Agent, while kind of wishy-washy specified, could represent either a new thread in the rendering process, or an entirely new process. Or, a new thread in an existing "Worker" process.

Either way, there is no guarantee that the new agent and the agent that is running the worker share a process.

In step 14, while executing in the new agent, we are supposed to fetch a worker classic/module script:

> 14. Obtain script by switching on the value of options's type member:
>
> "classic" -> [Fetch a classic worker script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetch-a-classic-worker-script) given url, outside settings, destination, inside settings, and with onComplete and performFetch as defined below.
> "module" -> [Fetch a module worker script graph](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetch-a-module-worker-script-tree) given url, outside settings, destination, the value of the credentials member of options, inside settings, and with onComplete and performFetch as defined below.

This implies that the `outside settings` variable is supposed to be the `fetchClient` EnvironmentSettingsObject for the fetch that will occur in the new Agent. However, the outside settings only exist in the owner Agent. How can we possibly pass that object to the fetch algorithm, when it belongs to a completely different realm, and a different Javascript VM?

Are implementers expected to pass some kind of representation of the relevant fields of the outside settings to the new agent and use that create a dummy Environment object that represents the owner?
